protocols.title: High Fever (>38.5°C / 101.3°F)
steps: Keep the patient in a cool, well-ventilated room.
Remove excess clothing and blankets.
Apply a cool (not cold) damp cloth to the forehead and wrists.
Encourage the patient to drink water, ORS, or clear fluids every 15 minutes.
Monitor temperature every 30 minutes.
If fever exceeds 40°C (104°F) or lasts more than 3 days, escalate to doctor immediately.

otc_medications.name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
otc_medications.warning: Do NOT exceed stated dose. Avoid in liver disease.

protocols.refer_if: Fever > 40°C, or any red flag symptom present, or no improvement after 2 days.

protocols.title: Minor Cuts & Wounds
steps: Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water before touching the wound.
Apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth to stop bleeding (hold for 5–10 minutes).
Once bleeding stops, rinse the wound under clean running water for 5 minutes.
Gently clean around the wound with an antiseptic wipe (from outer edge inward).
Apply antiseptic cream (e.g., Betadine) to the wound.
Cover with a sterile adhesive bandage or dressing.
Change dressing daily or when wet/dirty.
Check for signs of infection daily (redness, warmth, pus, swelling).

otc_medications.name: Povidone-Iodine (Betadine) solution/ointment
otc_medications.adult_dose: Apply topically to clean wound 1–2 times daily
otc_medications.child_dose: Same as adult — avoid on newborns
otc_medications.warning: Do not use inside deep puncture wounds.

red_flags: Deep or gaping wound (may need stitches)
Wound caused by an animal bite
protocols.refer_if: Wound is deep, won't stop bleeding after 10 minutes, or shows infection signs.

protocols.title: Dehydration / Diarrhoea
steps: Assess severity: mild (thirsty), moderate (dry mouth, less urine), severe (sunken eyes, confusion).
For mild/moderate: Begin Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) immediately.
ORS preparation: 1 litre of safe/boiled water + 6 teaspoons sugar + 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Adult: Give 200–400ml ORS after each loose stool.
Child under 5: Give 75ml/kg ORS over 4 hours.
Continue normal feeding. Breastfeeding mothers should continue.
Do NOT give anti-diarrhoeal drugs to children under 5.
Monitor urine output — improvement means treatment is working.

otc_medications.name: ORS Sachet (WHO formula)
otc_medications.adult_dose: 1 sachet dissolved in 1L water. 200–400ml after each stool.
otc_medications.child_dose: 75ml/kg in first 4 hours, then 10ml/kg after each stool
otc_medications.warning: Always use safe water. Discard prepared solution after 24 hours.

otc_medications.name: Zinc Sulfate (for children)
otc_medications.child_dose: Under 6 months: 10mg/day for 10–14 days. Over 6 months: 20mg/day for 10–14 days
otc_medications.warning: Zinc reduces diarrhoea duration in children. Do not overdose.

protocols.refer_if: Severe dehydration, bloody stool, child unable to drink, or no improvement in 24 hours.

protocols.title: Minor Burns (1st Degree)
steps: IMMEDIATELY cool the burn: run cool (NOT ice cold) water over it for 10–20 minutes.
Remove jewellery or tight clothing near the burn BEFORE swelling starts.
Do NOT apply butter, oil, toothpaste, or ice — these worsen the burn.
After cooling, cover loosely with a clean non-stick bandage or cling film.
Give pain relief if needed (paracetamol).
Keep the wound clean and dry. Change dressing daily.
Do NOT break any blisters — this increases infection risk.

otc_medications.name: Paracetamol
otc_medications.warning: For pain management only. Seek care for large or deep burns.

red_flags: Burn larger than palm of hand
Burn on face, hands, feet, genitals, or joints
protocols.refer_if: Any burn larger than a 5cm diameter, or ANY 2nd/3rd degree burn, or burns on sensitive areas.

protocols.title: Snake Bite Emergency
steps: KEEP THE PATIENT CALM AND STILL. Movement spreads venom faster.
Lay the patient down with the bitten limb BELOW the level of the heart.
Remove rings, watches, or tight clothing near the bite site immediately.
Clean the bite area gently with soap and water if available.
Immobilise the bitten limb using a splint or improvised sling.
DO NOT cut the wound, suck out venom, apply tourniquet, or apply ice.
Mark the edge of swelling with a pen and note the time.
TRANSPORT TO HOSPITAL IMMEDIATELY — time is critical for anti-venom.
Try to note the snake description (colour, pattern) but do NOT catch or kill it.
red_flags: Bleeding from bite or other sites
protocols.refer_if: ALL snake bites must be referred to a hospital immediately, regardless of symptoms.

protocols.title: Choking (Airway Obstruction)
steps: Ask loudly: 'Are you choking?' If they can speak or cough — encourage them to keep coughing.
If they CANNOT speak, cough, or breathe — ACT IMMEDIATELY.
Stand behind the person and lean them slightly forward.
Give 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades with heel of your hand.
If back blows fail, perform 5 ABDOMINAL THRUSTS (Heimlich Manoeuvre):
→ Stand behind them. Place fist (thumb-side in) just above navel.
→ Grab fist with other hand. Give 5 sharp inward-and-upward thrusts.
Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until object clears or patient loses consciousness.
If unconscious: Lower carefully to floor and begin CPR. Call for emergency help.
red_flags: Object not clearing after multiple attempts
protocols.refer_if: If object does not clear after 3–4 cycles of back blows and abdominal thrusts — emergency transport immediately.

protocols.title: Suspected Malaria
steps: Conduct Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) if available in the clinic kit.
Document symptoms: cyclical fever, chills, headache, muscle aches, nausea.
Keep patient cool and hydrated (ORS or water).
Give Paracetamol for fever and pain management.
Do NOT start anti-malarial drugs without confirming diagnosis via RDT or lab.
Refer patient to doctor for confirmed diagnosis and treatment plan.
Educate patient/family on mosquito bite prevention.

otc_medications.name: Paracetamol (symptomatic relief only)
otc_medications.warning: Paracetamol manages symptoms ONLY. Anti-malarials require a doctor's prescription.

protocols.refer_if: Positive RDT result, severe symptoms, young children, pregnant women — IMMEDIATE referral.
Symptoms persist beyond 48 hours or any red flag sign is present.
steps: Keep patient calm and comfortable.
Monitor vital signs (temperature, pulse, breathing).
Ensure patient is well hydrated.
If symptoms worsen or do not improve in 24 hours, seek medical attention.
protocols.title: Fever Me Kiya Kare
